# SSH-006: Logins are limited with AllowUsers or AllowGroups

- **Group:** SSH
- **Severity when it fails:** low
- **Root:** the full result needs `sudo`. Without root this check reports `unknown`, never a pass.

## Why it matters

Without an allow list, any account that gains a key or a password (a service account, a forgotten user, an account a package created) may log in. Listing the accounts that should log in turns every other account into a refusal.

## Verify by hand

```sh
sudo sshd -T | grep -Ei '^allow(users|groups)'
```

## How to fix it

Add AllowUsers with the accounts that log in (or AllowGroups with a group such as sshusers).

## What a fix can break

Every account not listed is refused, including automation users; list them all before reloading.

Run `stackward explain SSH-006` for the same text in your terminal. [All checks](index.md).
